I Want You Hard
notes: “first up we're going to hear from the legendary and very sexed up ebm producer from denmark leather strip ... We're going to hear a song called I Want You Hard”
Track 8 on 'The Rebirth of Agony' (1996), Danish EBM artist Claus Larsen's project.

rows.title: Leather Jacket II
notes: “Deer Hunter there with Leather Jacket 2 from their album Monomania.”
Standout fuzzed-out garage track from Deerhunter's 2013 album 'Monomania'.

rows.title: My Tunnel
notes: Darby Crash/Pat Smear-penned Germs track, released on the 'MIA: The Complete Anthology' compilation.
“we're going to hear from Billiam, who's such a sweetheart”
Australian DIY garage/'autismcore' solo artist, prolific on labels like Goodbye Boozy and Erste Theke Tontraeger; no specific title was announced.

rows.title: Leather Gunn
notes: “At the top, we had Alien Nosejob... A track called Leather Gun”
Track 2 on Melbourne artist Jake Robertson's 'Paint It Clear' cassette (2024), Devo-ish new wave cut.
“we're going to hear from Sportsbra as well”
Sydney band with a Bandcamp page (sportsbralovesyou); released LP 'Talk It Out'. No specific title was announced.

rows.title: Wild Strawberries
notes: “The wonderful, strange world of Jandek there. A track called Wild Strawberries off his album 6 and 6.”
Track 5 (6:02) on Jandek's 1981 Corwood Industries album 'Six and Six'.

rows.title: Women, Leather and Hell
notes: “That was Black Metal Pioneer's Venom with Women, Leather, and Hell.”
Early Venom (black metal pioneers) track, collected on the 'From Heaven to the Unknown' compilation.
“That was a band from the 2000s in Melbourne... called Hinge, but with the period at the start, I guess you'd maybe say Dot Hinge.”
2000s Melbourne band (period-prefixed name), played Melbourne's Hi-Fi in 2008; no specific title was announced.

rows.title: Colin's First Ride
notes: “you just heard the cue of the track was called Colin's First Ride”
1:50 cue from the 'Pillion' (A24) original soundtrack, released Dec 2025.

rows.title: Red Pleather
notes: Track from Melbourne synth-pop artist Pikelet's (Evelyn Ida Morris) 'Stem' album.
